message.content: Lions mate in a relatively straightforward but highly social manner. Male lions typically form coalitions—groups of related males that defend a pride together. When a coalition mates with a pride, they take turns courting females. Courtship involves scent marking, vocalizing (roaring), and physical displays such as head-butting or licking. Once a female accepts a male’s advances, she will mount him and the male will mount her from behind. The actual copulation lasts only a few minutes, but it can happen repeatedly over several days. After mating, the male may stay with the pride for a short period to guard the females and young, but he usually leaves once the cubs are born and the females begin to raise them.
